channel.title: Morgenlinie
channel.description: Lucas's morning news digest, summarised by Claude.

item.title: Qatar urges the US and Iran not to wait for a “perfect moment” on a deal
item.description:
Global headlines. Developing, reports differ. Reported by Al Jazeera

Speaking at Oxford, Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani called on Washington and Tehran to reach a peace deal without delay. Iran's IRNA reported two missiles striking Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, and semi-official outlets reported no casualties.

Read at Al Jazeera

item.title: Paraguay's Senate removes Peña, and Pedro Alliana is sworn in
item.description:
Global headlines. Developing. Reported by Al Jazeera and AP

The Senate voted 44 of 45 to remove Santiago Peña over the Ueno Bank collapse, and Alliana became the 53rd president on Friday. Peña is under house arrest, at least 27 people face criminal charges, and his lawyers say the impeachment timetable was too short.

Read at Al Jazeera

item.title: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff
item.description:
Global headlines. Developing. Reported by Al Jazeera

Trump called Miller “one of my most trusted advisors” on Truth Social; he takes over from Susie Wiles from Monday. The change comes as Democrats prepare to take control of the House and Senate in January, where investigations into Miller are expected.

Read at Al Jazeera

item.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years
item.description:
Global headlines. Reported by Reuters via The Standard

He was convicted over the starvation deaths of 190 children and one adult linked to Shakahola Forest, where Kenya's rights commission counts 448 bodies. Twenty-eight accomplices received 10 to 160 years, and the defence says it will appeal.

Read at The Standard

item.title: US measles cases pass 5,000, the most since 1991
item.description:
Global headlines. Death counts disputed. Reported by Al Jazeera

The CDC reports 5,182 confirmed cases this year, about 59% among children and teens, as kindergarten vaccination coverage fell from 95.2% to 92.4%. The CDC counts four deaths, while Pennsylvania reports six in that state alone.

Read at Al Jazeera

item.title: Union settles on Ilse Aigner as candidate for Bundespräsidentin
item.description:
German politics. Not yet official. Reported by Tagesspiegel and ZDFheute

Tagesspiegel confirmed from the CDU leadership that the Union has agreed on the CSU Landtag president, who would be Germany's first female head of state; the CDU Präsidium meets on Sunday evening and party bodies on Monday. SPD leader Lars Klingbeil said the SPD would “das begrüßen und unterstützen”, and CDU, CSU and SPD have a majority in the Bundesversammlung on 30 January.

Tagesspiegel · ZDFheute

item.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Siegmund eyes extra ballots, CDU to judge AfD motions case by case
item.description:
German politics. Reported by Tagesspiegel, with dpa and AFP

AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund, who needs three votes from other groups in December's vote for minister-president, now leaves a second or third ballot open: “Wir haben jetzt eine historische Chance.” CDU leader Sven Schulze said “Wir werden von Fall zu Fall entscheiden” on AfD motions, while the party's Unvereinbarkeitsbeschluss still applies.

Tagesspiegel (dpa) · Tagesspiegel (AFP)

item.title: CDU threatens to block the planned income tax reform
item.description:
German politics. Reported by Tagesspiegel (AFP)

Mathias Middelberg called the plan “nicht zustimmungsfähig” without a workable option model for partnerships. The reform would raise the top rate from 45 to 47% and cut corporate tax from 15 to 10%.

Read at Tagesspiegel

item.title: Bundestag toughens penalties for K.-o.-Tropfen
item.description:
German politics. Reported by taz

Drugging someone for rape, sexual coercion or robbery is now treated like using a dangerous tool, raising the minimum sentence from three to five years. CDU/CSU, SPD, Greens and Linke voted for the bill from Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig, and the AfD abstained.

Read at taz

item.title: PP gives mixed answers on meetings between its lawyer and Koldo García
item.description:
Spanish politics. Allegation, denied. Reported by elDiario.es

On Koldo García's claim that PP lawyer Alberto Durán offered him money for information against the government, PP spokesperson Ester Muñoz said “no ha habido ninguna reunión”, while the party leadership answered “No lo sé” on meetings but “con ofrecimientos seguro que no”. Koldo's lawyer has given the court two invoices totalling €242,000, and the PSOE says it is studying legal action.

Read at elDiario.es

item.title: Judge rejects malversación charge against Zapatero in the jewels case
item.description:
Spanish politics. Court decision. Reported by elDiario.es

Judge José Luis Calama declined Anticorrupción's request to charge the former prime minister with misuse of public funds. Zapatero remains under investigation for a tax offence, which may have expired, and for smuggling.

Read at elDiario.es

item.title: Guardia Civil estimates 88,146 migrants returned after the Ceuta entry
item.description:
Spanish politics. Official estimate. Reported by Público (EFE)

An internal report dated 27 October says “aproximadamente 88.146” people may have gone back to Morocco after the mass entry of 30 and 31 July, a higher figure than the government gave before. It also counts 862 rescues and 90 deaths, as the Audiencia Nacional investigation continues.

Read at Público

item.title: No contractor for the Eifelstrecke overhead lines, so DB changes its plans
item.description:
Rail and public transport. DB InfraGO statement, reported by Bahnblogstelle

“Für den Einbau der Oberleitungen fehlt weiter ein Auftragnehmer,” despite repeated tenders, while work on 10 tunnels and 56 bridges continues from March 2027. In 2027 there will be no trains between Gerolstein and Euskirchen, and continuous service is expected again from the end of 2028.

Read at Bahnblogstelle

item.title: Frankfurt Hauptbahnhof gets an extra platform track
item.description:
Rail and public transport. DB statement, reported by Bahnblogstelle

A new track 25 with a step-free island platform is to ease the station and separate traffic, benefiting RB10, RB12, RB22 and RE20 services via Frankfurt-Höchst. The station stays open during the works, and no cost or completion date was given.

Read at Bahnblogstelle

item.title: IAG now expects its first Boeing 777-9 in 2028
item.description:
Global aviation. Reported by FlightGlobal, paywalled summary only

The British Airways parent also expects to take 12 rather than 16 aircraft of other types this year. It is a further sign of the 777X delays that are already reshaping fleet plans at other European groups.

Read at FlightGlobal

item.title: Southwest 737 loses an engine after take-off and diverts to LAX
item.description:
Global aviation. Reported by Simple Flying

Flight 3396 from Santa Ana to San Jose, a 19-year-old 737-700 with 97 people aboard, declared an emergency and landed at Los Angeles after 38 minutes. No injuries were reported.

Read at Simple Flying

item.title: Southwest 737 MAX flew 44 times with undetected storm damage
item.description:
Global aviation. NTSB final report, reported by AirlineGeeks

The tail damage came from gusts of up to 73 knots at New Orleans in May 2024 and “went undetected through a scheduled maintenance check”. Boeing has since required a special inspection after winds of 65 knots.

Read at AirlineGeeks

item.title: BKA seeks another suspect over explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle
item.description:
Global aviation. Dates unclear. Reported by aeroTELEGRAPH

Federal police have issued a public appeal for an unknown person seen on an e-bike near the airport, where an explosive-laden drone was found near the Antonov An-225; two suspects have already been identified. The article dates the find to early August, and only this one outlet was checked.

Read at aeroTELEGRAPH

item.title: Democrats win both chambers of the US Congress
item.description:
Global headlines. Developing. Reported by taz

taz's live blog, citing US projections, reports Democrats took the House and flipped the Senate with wins including Texas, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa. As of 07:30 CET, Michigan and Alaska were uncalled, Maine was still counting, and no final House total was available. It leaves President Trump facing a Democratic Congress for his last two years.

Read at taz

item.title: Iran calls US reply on Hormuz “unconvincing” as Trump confirms a strike
item.description:
Global headlines. Developing. Reported by Al Jazeera, with Reuters content

Mohsen Rezaei said Washington must “fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions”. Trump called a strike on an Iranian anti-aircraft facility a “minor attack”, while US media report plans for strikes that could begin as early as Wednesday. Qatar says both sides remain committed to talks. Iranian claims about tankers hitting mines are unverified.

Read at Al Jazeera

item.title: Trump says US will end military aid to Israel from 2027
item.description:
Global headlines. Reported by Euronews

He said the roughly $4 billion a year would stop while arms sales continue, and that Netanyahu first proposed the idea. The current deal runs to 2028. Netanyahu's office had not commented when Euronews published.

Read at Euronews

item.title: Ebola death toll passes 5,300
item.description:
Global headlines. Reported by Al Jazeera, with AFP and Reuters

Africa CDC data put deaths at 5,376, nearly all in DR Congo, in an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain, which has no approved vaccine or treatment. About 10,444 people have been infected across DR Congo, Uganda and Kenya.

Read at Al Jazeera

item.title: Reiche's fuel price cap draft heads to cabinet under SPD fire
item.description:
German politics. Reported by taz

The cabinet is due to vote on Wednesday. A cap could apply only if German prices rise at least 5 points more than the EU average for three straight weeks, which taz says has not happened in ten years. SPD deputy leader Anke Rehlinger wants the draft revised, and the Greens and Die Linke want a windfall tax. The current fuel tax cut ends on 1 January.

Read at taz

item.title: Merz: the next president “has to be a woman”
item.description:
German politics. Reported by AFP via The Local, and taz

He said so at a closed CDU meeting, according to party sources, and named no one. The CSU has nominated Ilse Aigner, whom taz says the SPD supports. CDU bodies should decide early next week. Sources differ on the date: AFP says 30 January, taz says February.

The Local · taz

item.title: Merz hosts Zelensky before Abu Dhabi talks
item.description:
German politics. Reported by taz and Al Jazeera

Merz said “Es ist Zeit für ein Ende des Krieges” and that Europe wants a decisive role. US-brokered talks are set for 10–11 November. Ukrainian officials say at least 31 people died in Russia's strike on an aid centre in Komyshuvakha.

taz · Al Jazeera

item.title: Gas plants take every contract in first capacity auction
item.description:
German politics. Reported by taz

The Bundesnetzagentur awarded 5,160 MW across 11 contracts, six to LEAG and three to RWE, with nothing for storage. Reiche called it a “great success”, while BUND estimates the cost at over €12 billion over 15 years, paid through an electricity levy.

Read at taz

item.title: Puente's exit leaves Sánchez to fill Transport weeks before 29N
item.description:
Spanish politics. Reported by EFE via Infobae, and Público

Puente stays until his resignation takes effect. Sánchez must then name a new minister or give another minister the ordinary running of the department. Puente says he bore no direct responsibility for Urda, which killed 69 people. He will not stand, though Público says his name stays on the published Valladolid list.

Infobae (EFE) · Público

item.title: Adif works council agrees a rail safety strike for 17 November
item.description:
Spanish politics. Reported by EFE via Público

The strike is not yet formally called. Renfe's works council was also weighing a stoppage, and a rally is planned for 16 November.

Read at Público

item.title: PP and Vox clash with unions over the 11N general strike
item.description:
Spanish politics. Reported by elDiario.es

Feijóo called the housing-focused strike “un grave error” after Urda, and Abascal said Vox would “tomar nota”. CCOO and UGT called the remarks a threat. The PP denies coordinating with Vox.

Read at elDiario.es

item.title: Judge Llarena closes the Puigdemont investigation
item.description:
Spanish politics. Reported by EFE via Público

The case now goes to the Supreme Court's criminal chamber, which will decide on dismissal under the amnesty law. EFE describes the step as largely formal.

Read at Público

item.title: Long-distance punctuality stays below 60% in October
item.description:
Rail and public transport. Reported by Bahnblogstelle, from dpa

It reached 56.2%, about four points up on September but short of Evelyn Palla's 60% target for the year. Construction sites and infrastructure faults are the main causes cited.

Read at Bahnblogstelle

item.title: “Robuster Fahrplan” commission starts work on fewer trains
item.description:
Rail and public transport. Reported by Bahnblogstelle and taz, from dpa

DB InfraGO's expert panel met from 3 November, with proposals due in the new year. Member Enak Ferlemann has floated hourly instead of half-hourly Berlin–Hamburg trains. Allianz pro Schiene warns of fuller trains, and Die Güterbahnen rejects blanket cuts.

Bahnblogstelle · taz

item.title: Deutschlandticket sales fee dispute goes to a vote on 10 November
item.description:
Rail and public transport. Reported by Bahnblogstelle

VRR chief Oliver Wittke opposes raising the fee from €2.87 to €3.15, saying DB would benefit most. The VDV says the Bundeskartellamt set the principle of the sales incentive.

Read at Bahnblogstelle

item.title: First Hamburg U5 tunnel section reaches shell completion
item.description:
Rail and public transport. Reported by Zughalt.de

The roughly 1.5 km stretch runs from west of Sengelmannstraße to City Nord. Test runs are planned from 2028 and opening for the end of 2029. A public tunnel tour takes place on 14 November.

Read at Zughalt.de

item.title: Lufthansa signs deal for 44.9% of TAP
item.description:
Global aviation. Lufthansa press release, reported by Simple Flying

The initial price is €1.025 billion, and the stake could reach 49.9% with a maximum of €1.2 billion. Lisbon would become the group's seventh hub. EU approval is required: Simple Flying expects closing in 2028, while Lufthansa's statement gives no date.

Lufthansa Group · Simple Flying

item.title: Lufthansa narrows its outlook and warns of double-digit fare rises
item.description:
Global aviation. Reported by The Local and FlightGlobal

Core profit guidance is now €1.7–2.0 billion, with its 2026 fuel bill seen at €9.3 billion. Finance chief Till Streichert said: “Ticket prices will increase by double digits next year.” Third-quarter net profit rose 30%, but adjusted EBIT fell 11% at the network airlines.

The Local · FlightGlobal

item.title: First Lufthansa 777-9 misses summer 2027
item.description:
Global aviation. Reported by FlightGlobal

The delivery has slipped to the second quarter, and the airline has activated its contingency plan. It expects a low single-digit number of deliveries in 2027.

Read at FlightGlobal

item.title: US-bound travellers must attest they have not been in DR Congo
item.description:
Global aviation. Reported by Simple Flying

The CDC order took effect for flights departing from 23:59 EST on 3 November, covers crew and runs until 18 December unless changed. Anyone who refuses to sign is denied boarding.

Read at Simple Flying

item.title: French gigabyte tax could cost VLC's makers over €1 million a year
item.description:
Wednesday topic: open source. Reported by It's FOSS

The National Assembly backed an amendment charging €0.055 per GB delivered to French subscribers, with no explicit exemption for free software. VideoLAN gives the estimate before a revenue cap, and author Laurent Lhardit says the cap protects small players. The article does not describe later steps.

Read at It's FOSS

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 runs late under an LLM bug load
item.description:
Wednesday topic: open source. Reported by LWN.net and Phoronix

Developer Robert Haas ties the delay to the project's focus on quality, and to LLM-found bugs and patches that still need human review. Phoronix says November is the earliest date.

LWN.net · Phoronix

item.title: Fedora Linux 45 ships after two delays
item.description:
Wednesday topic: open source. Reported by It's FOSS

Released on 3 November with Linux 7.2, GNOME 51, Plasma 6.7 and Podman 6.1. It also replaces fbcon with kmscon for virtual consoles.

Read at It's FOSS
